name: The Den
summary: In southwestern Durotar, young orcs and trolls gather at the sheltered Den in the heart of the Valley of Trials. It is their main base, where they train in arms and magic before setting out into the wider world.

sections.title: Cradle of the Horde
sections.body: The Den is an austere proving ground, carved into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials. Inside its shadowed halls, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters answer to veterans such as Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. They receive their first combat lessons, supplies, and rites of passage, preparing for Durotar's harshness and the struggles facing the new Horde.

sections.title: A Watchful Outpost
sections.body: The Den houses class trainers and merchants who provide provisions. From this field outpost, overseers send recruits to cull local beasts and aggressive quilboars. They keep a strict watch over the valley.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Den?
faq.answer: The Den is the central base and training ground in the Valley of Trials. Novice orcs and Darkspear trolls learn basic class techniques, buy provisions, and receive assignments meant to prove their loyalty and readiness to fight for the Horde.

faq.q: Who runs things inside the Den?
faq.answer: Veteran overseers such as Gornek and Foreman Thazz'ril supervise the Den. Spiritual and magical mentors, including Zureetha Fargaze and Canaga Earthcaller, instruct the newest warriors and mystics.

faq.q: Can you learn primary professions here?
faq.answer: No. The Den has basic class trainers and general equipment merchants. To study primary trades such as Blacksmithing, Leatherworking, or Mining, travel north to Razor Hill or continue to Orgrimmar.

angles.text: Every young orc begins at the Den, leaving behind the complacency of the internment camps and blood haze. Discipline and labor are how you earn your place.
After the Darkspear Isles were devastated, young Darkspear trolls began training in the Den beside their orc allies. Under the Horde's banner, you must prove your mettle.
